_README: Direct-program merchant rates for the merchants appearing in the corpus.
HARD RULE 2: every rate carries source_url and fetched_at. Every rate here
was read off the MERCHANT'S OWN public affiliate-recruitment page, rendered
in Chromium with the honest DisclosedBot user-agent and robots.txt checked
per host. `quotes` carries the page's exact wording so a third party can
recompute the parse from the same URL. No rate here came from a blog, an
affiliate-network directory, a coupon aggregator, or model recall.
rate_kind — what the page actually published:
point   one unambiguous number for all sales -> `rate` is set
range   a floor and a ceiling -> `rate` is null, bounds in rate_min/max
cap     'up to X%' with no floor -> `rate` is null, rate_max only
none    the page describes a program but publishes no percentage
not_applicable  the host is not a merchant at all -> no rate can exist
WHY A RANGE YIELDS rate: null. SPEC-scoring.md §0.1 defines r_i as the
rate THIS PUBLISHER earns on this pick, null only when the rate is not
public. A published band of 4%-7% does not tell us which tier a given
publisher sits in — that is negotiated privately — so the rate for that
publisher is not public and r_i is null. Recording the midpoint would be
inventing a number, which is exactly what HARD RULE 2 forbids.
A null with checked_urls is an honest row, not a gap. It records that we
looked, where we looked, and when.
classification_only: true marks a row that exists to say a host will NEVER
be priced by a rate card — a publisher property, a social or citation link,
a CDN, or a redirect/network host. That is a different fact from "we have
not looked yet", and it is the fact the census needs in order to stop
counting a newsletter sign-up as an unfetched rate. Such a row NEVER
reclassifies a link: whether a link was badged monetized was decided
upstream by the classifier and is untouched here.
A row may also be null because we were BLOCKED rather than because the
merchant published nothing. Those two are stated differently and must stay
that way — "the rate is not public" is a claim about the merchant, while
"not observable from our egress" or "the merchant blocks our crawler" is a
claim about us. Recording the second as the first would be a false
statement about a named company.
Rates change without notice. Re-check before any published score.
fetched_from_geo — the geography our crawl egress was in when the row was
fetched or checked. It is on EVERY row because a rate can be geo-specific and
a row read from one country is not evidence about another. Ours is CA.
reason `geo_gated_fetched_from_CA` — the merchant serves geo-specific pages
and, from a Canadian egress, the US page is not reachable: the request is
geo-redirected to a Canadian page or answered with a country selector. This is
a claim about OUR VANTAGE POINT, not about the merchant, and it is deliberately
distinct from a 403 or a timeout, which are different claims again. The prose
originally recorded is preserved in `reason_prose`.
reason `program_pays_services_only` — the merchant's own page defines the
program as covering a product class that the picks in this corpus are not in.
It is a RATE statement and never a classification: m_i is decided upstream.
categories[] — a merchant that publishes a per-category rate card carries one
entry per published row, each with its OWN source_url and fetched_at, because
HARD RULE 2 binds per rate and not per merchant.

WHAT IT WAS LOOKING FOR. SPEC v0.6.12 §0.1.5, ratified one commit before the probe ran with an
EMPTY list: a merchant whose own site STATES it operates no affiliate or referral program
publishes a rate, and the rate is zero. That is a different fact from `no_affiliate_page_found`,
which is OUR failure to find a page and licenses nothing.
EXACTLY ONE MERCHANT QUALIFIES: Mullvad. The extractor captured 20 candidate sentences across 9
merchants and NINETEEN OF THEM ARE FALSE POSITIVES — 'There's no cap on commissions' (DreamHost),

disagrees with its card, this file is stale — regenerate it.

_README: Vertical -> MERCHANT fee category, for merchants that publish a per-category
rate card on their own site. The direct-merchant counterpart of
amazon-category-map.json, and it follows that file's discipline exactly.
EVERY mapping carries basis "assumption — verify via product breadcrumb".
No merchant publishes a vertical-to-category crosswalk, so the
vertical -> category edge is OUR inference and is not evidence. The RATE on
the far side of that edge is fetched, cited and timestamped in
merchants.json; the edge itself is not.
ambiguous: the product could sit in more than one of the merchant's own
published categories, and those categories pay DIFFERENT rates. Under
SPEC-scoring.md §0.1.1 that is a BAND, not a choice for us to make: r_i is
the published minimum across the candidates and rate_max carries the
ceiling. Choosing one category would be inventing a rate.
rate_robust_to_ambiguity: the candidates all pay the same, so the
assumption cannot move r_i and verification is not on the critical path.
SCOPE. A vertical is mapped ONLY where this corpus actually contains picks
reaching that merchant. Mapping verticals we have never observed would be
writing assumptions nobody has checked against a real article. Verticals we
looked at and REFUSED to map are in unmapped_verticals with the reason.
merchants.json is authoritative for the rates. If a rate here disagrees
with the card, this file is stale — regenerate it against the card.

notes: Shipped as DATA, never as code. Manifest V3 forbids remote code execution and this file is never evaluated.
Every rate row carries its own source_url and fetched_at. A rate without provenance is not a rate (CLAUDE.md HARD RULE 2).
medianRho is present only for a publisher over the SPEC §2.2 threshold of 20 qualifying articles. Below it, the state is carried and no number is.
Signatures marked verified: false classify at `likely`, never `confirmed`. Host patterns a rater declined are not in this file at all.
This bundle contains no corpus, no links, no labels and no article ids.
redirectorHosts is a refuse-to-fetch list, not a signature list. A host in it is badged by nothing and classifies exactly as it would if the list were empty.
resolutions is HASH-KEYED: sha256(url) -> destination, with no URL in the file. A client that already holds a URL can look it up; nobody can enumerate the list from this file.

resolutions_truncated false means the whole table shipped and a client MUST make no network call to resolve anything. It goes true only when the table exceeds the byte cap, and only then is /v1/resolve the fallback.

A resolution row carries its status. robots_disallowed (an operator refused and we honoured it), blocked (we were turned away), not_a_redirect and resolved are four findings and are never merged into one absence.

No resolution was obtained by a reader’s browser. Every row was observed server-side, cookieless, honest-UA, HEAD first, and the destination itself was never requested (CLAUDE.md privacy architecture point 3).
